title: Short feedback, or fix the item
statement: Keep corrective feedback short and aimed at the error; a correction that needs more is new teaching, so fix the item or its placement instead.
example: One later course never lets feedback run past 60 words.
detail: A second-round outside review of a Grade 3 reading course found corrective feedback on many wrong answers but far too long, at times longer than the passage itself, and said a grade-3 child would not read it (`grade3-reading/artifacts/op-taxonomy-calibration-2026-07-10/r2-feedback-docx-converted.txt`). The reading project's audit of its practice principles records the rule that when the feedback needed to correct a response is longer and more complex than the original instruction, the item has crossed the acquisition boundary, so the item or its placement is fixed, not the feedback (`grade3-reading/artifacts/team-direction-2026-09-09/research/02-current-brainlift-spov-audit.md`). A later Grade 5 course's authoring rules set feedback at a 40-word target, never more than 60 (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/LESSON-AUTHORING-PLAYBOOK.md`). Feedback is never longer or harder than the passage or the teaching it corrects, and its length is checked in code.
against: It is a rule borrowed from a practice framework; nothing in these sources measures it. The word counts are a proposed lint for one grade band, not a built check. The lint is a local reference implementation, not wired into any repository or pipeline (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/tooling/ti-courseplans-2169d1f/scripts/lane-tools/op-lint/README.md`). none found; the 40- and 60-word figures were set for grade 3 readers (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/instruction-quality-standard.md`). Enforced only when more than a fifth of items fail: 'feedback_quality -> 0.0 when >20% of items-with-feedback carry a hard defect.' (`shadow-bench`, git commit 9c9d00c, line 15). The per-option check is 'Report-only by design' (git commit 6e7af07, line 22). The word limits are one team's bar, not a measured threshold.

The LLM feedback_quality metric checks only that feedback explains WHY; it never measures length or mechanics, so a wall-of-text explanation (even longer than the passage) passes. Adds a shared deterministic lint mirroring the academics bar: <=40-word target / 60-word hard cap, "longer than the passage" defect, bare-generic
- per-distractor feedback: each wrong option should carry its own non-generic feedback (bare "Incorrect." / absent → flagged).
Fail: feedback is absent on the majority of items, OR feedback consists only of "Correct!" / "Incorrect!" with no explanation.

Where a correction needs a home and no single item can carry it, put it in the guide's own voice as a plain statement near the vocabulary work ("say it here"), not buried in feedback.
